Reimbursement Overview

$110

Maximum reimbursement per participant

### Bus

Public transportation buses

### Plane

Commercial airline flights

### Ride-Sharing

Uber, Lyft, and similar services

### Taxi

Traditional taxi services

### Rental Vehicle

Car rental services

- Only the person named on the receipt can be reimbursed
- Verification of initial departure point required
- Digital receipts are accepted for arrival trip only

Reimbursements may take up to 2 months to process after the event.

Upload your receipts to the reimbursement page by going to the bottom of your profile page and clicking the Submit Reimbursement button.

# America250 Backs College Entrepreneurs with Re-Opening of "America's Startup" National Competition

Aug 17, 2026, 11:30 ET

Following a Successful Spring Pilot, National Collegiate Competition Expands with Over $1 Million Prize Pool, Non-Dilutive Funding, and Mentorship 

WASHINGTON, Aug. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Following the success of its inaugural competition earlier this year, America250, the nonpartisan organization charged by Congress with leading the national celebration of the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence, today announced the return of America's Startup, an expanded national collegiate competition designed to identify, support, and celebrate the country's most promising undergraduate entrepreneurs and early-stage innovators.

 

 America250 Launches America's Startup Fall Program 

Applications are open August 17 through October 8, 2026, inviting undergraduate students (or the equivalent) enrolled at accredited U.S. colleges, universities, and trade schools to compete for a share of a $1 million total prize pool—including up to $50,000 in non-dilutive grant funding per team, national mentorship, and a live pitch finale in Washington, D.C.

Sponsored by the Ethics, Society, & Technology Initiatives and the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence (HAI)

Through the Tech Ethics & Policy Fellows Program, Stanford undergraduate students have the opportunity to engage in the technology field as it intersects with public policy and social impact. The program runs from April to October and includes a course on ethics, technology, and public policy, as well as a paid summer opportunity at a technology company, civil society organization, federal agency, or Congressional office. Fellows will also be matched with mentors from the technology, ethics, and public policy fields.

title: Milstein Travel Grant | Milstein Program in Technology and Humanity
text:
Milstein Travel Grant | Milstein Program in Technology and Humanity

# Milstein Travel Grant

Any time from sophomore to senior year, Milstein scholars can apply for up to $500 in funding to support travel related to academic or career development pursuits (for example, attending a conference, travel for research, traveling for an interview, etc.). Allowable expenses include hotel stays, plane tickets, and conference fees.

Students can apply for the fund only once while in the program. Proposals will be accepted on a rolling basis and funds will be disbursed as reimbursement after the proposed opportunity.

Students who are awarded travel grant funding must write a short reflection (1 page single-spaced) to be submitted no more than two weeks after the trip/experience.

## Application Guidelines

Students should submit the following materials as one .pdf file:

1. Estimated budget (feel free to use the blank budget calculation doc as a guide, or just create your own itemized budget) - students will be asked to save all receipts and submit them for reimbursement. The funding will be disbursed after the travel occurs.
2. Tentative travel itinerary
3. 1-2 paragraph description of why the funds are needed and how the opportunity will benefit your academic or career development.
4. Cover sheet with name, netID, major, where you are traveling and when you are traveling
5. Events

text:
Hudson River Trading CppCon Scholarship | CppCon

# Hudson River Trading CppCon Scholarship

Hudson River Trading’s (HRT) engineering culture is built on rigor, performance, and intellectual honesty. We write code to solve complex, real-time challenges at the intersection of computer science and global markets, and we believe that fostering deep technical expertise, curiosity, and diverse perspectives are essential to advancing the state of modern computing.

As part of this commitment, we are proud to partner with CppCon – the premier forum for the C++ community to share knowledge and explore language evolution – to support the next generation of C++ engineers who are passionate about building high-performance, reliable software. We are supporting CppCon’s mission of providing opportunities for C++ developers, researchers, and language contributors to learn from leading practitioners by offering a scholarship for select students to attend CppCon 2026.

Through this scholarship, we aim to help reduce barriers to attending CppCon and invest in students eager to grow as software engineers and quant researchers. We are looking for students who are not just users of C++, but genuinely curious about what happens “under the hood” – from memory models and concurrency to low-level hardware behavior – and who are excited by challenging problems, motivated by learning, and serious about building excellent software.

Student Travel Grants: 2026 LLVM Developers' Meeting

The LLVM Foundation is committed to diversity and education in the fields of compilers and tools, and supporting the long term health and growth of the LLVM Project. Therefore, the LLVM Foundation provides travel grants to students attending the LLVM Developers’ Meetings or other compilers and tools related educational conferences.

Applications are open for student travel grants to attend the 2026 LLVM Developers’ Meeting taking place October 27 - 28, 2026 (pre-conference sessions on October 26) at the Santa Clara Marriott.

The deadline for 2026 LLVM Dev Mtg applications is July 17, 2026.

The deadline for student grant applications has passed.

### Selection Criteria

Scholarship recipients are selected based on the following criteria:

- Participation with the LLVM Project or relevant work experience.
- Financial need.
- Priority may be given to those presenting a paper/work using LLVM or related sub-project at the conference/workshop.
- Priority may be given to underrepresented backgrounds, genders, and experiences to encourage broader participation in computer science and engineering.
- Priority may be given to those within the local travel region.
- Past recipients of LLVM Foundation travel grants may not be selected.

### Eligibility

# AnitaB.org Kamala Scholars

The AnitaB.org Kamala Scholars Program empowers the next generation of innovators by providing resources, mentorship, and access to Grace Hopper Celebration. 

Applications are now open! Apply by 11:59pm ET on September 8, 2026.

## About the Kamala Scholars Program

The Kamala Scholars Program is a year-long opportunity made possible through the generosity of an anonymous donor, in honor of a family member, and is dedicated to opening doors and creating pathways for 3rd- and 4th-year undergraduate students pursuing technical computing fields. AnitaB.org offers many opportunities to elevate the full diaspora of our community. This particular scholarship is focused exclusively on Black and Latine students, in alignment with the donor’s wishes. Each year, we welcome 125 students into the program.

### Scholars receive:

1

### Travel, Lodging & Transportation

Fully funded travel, lodging, and transportation to attend Grace Hopper Celebration

2

### AnitaB.org Membership

One year of Premium AnitaB.org Membership

3

### Career Coaching Sessions

10 one-on-one career coaching sessions for professional growth

As part of their commitment, selected scholars are required to attend GHC 26 in Anaheim, October 27-30, 2026, participate fully in their coaching sessions, and complete required program surveys.
